prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Neil L. Andersen dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Neil L. Andersen dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Neil L. Andersen of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles has dedicated temples on several continents. They include Lisbon Portugal (2019), Praia Cape Verde (2022), Brasília (2023) and Salvador (2024) in Brazil, and Farmington New Mexico (2025). On May 31, 2026, he dedicated Bacolod, the sixth dedicated temple in the Philippines.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country with exactly two dedicated temples.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with exactly two dedicated temples (as of October 2026).
prompts.summary: Several countries had exactly two dedicated temples as of October 2026. Examples include New Zealand (Hamilton and Auckland), Germany (Freiberg and Frankfurt), South Africa (Johannesburg and Durban) and Ecuador (Guayaquil and Quito). In the United Kingdom both temples, London and Preston, are in England.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London and Preston, both in England.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country with a land or city from the Genesis 10 Table of Nations whose site is agreed.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country with a land or city in the Genesis 10 Table of Nations whose site is agreed
prompts.summary: Genesis 10 lists the families of Noah's sons Shem, Ham and Japheth, from whom the nations spread after the flood (Genesis 10:1, 32). Many names match real places: Mizraim is Egypt, Javan is Greece, Elam and Madai are in Iran, and Babel and Nineveh are in Iraq. Sidon is called Canaan's firstborn (Genesis 10:15).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Babel, Erech, Accad, Nineveh and Calah are named (Genesis 10:10-11).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Mizraim is the Hebrew name for Egypt.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Gerar, on the Canaanite border between Sidon and Gaza (Genesis 10:19), lies in Israel whichever proposed site is right.

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Javan, son of Japheth, is the Hebrew name for the Greeks.

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Elam and Madai (the Medes) were in today's Iran.

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Gaza (Genesis 10:19) lies in the Gaza Strip.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: The Arvadites and Hamathites point to Arwad and Hama.

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Kittim takes its name from Kition, a city on Cyprus.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country where Paul set foot in Acts, or that held a church he wrote to or a place he meant to visit.
prompts.text_original: A present-day country where Paul set foot in Acts, or that held a church he wrote to or a place he planned to visit
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: After his conversion, Paul preached in Damascus and then spent years carrying the gospel across the Roman world. Born in Tarsus in today's Turkey, he founded churches at Philippi, Thessalonica and Corinth in Greece and later wrote letters to them. Acts ends with Paul living under guard in Rome, and he told the Romans he hoped to go on to Spain (Romans 15:24, 28).

answers.name: Greece
answers.fact: Paul founded churches at Philippi, Thessalonica and Corinth, was jailed at Philippi and wrote to all three (Acts 16-18).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Paul landed at Ptolemais and was held two years at Caesarea (Acts 21:7-8; 24:27).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: Paul was born in Tarsus, was stoned at Lystra and wrote to the Galatians, Ephesians and Colossians (Acts 14:19; 21:39).

answers.name: Cyprus
answers.fact: Paul preached in the synagogues of Salamis and went on to Paphos (Acts 13:5-6).

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Paul wrote his longest letter to Rome and lived there two years under guard (Acts 28:16, 30).

answers.name: Malta
answers.fact: Paul spent three months on Malta after the shipwreck (Acts 28:1-11).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Paul preached in the Damascus synagogues and escaped over the wall in a basket (Acts 9:20, 25).

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Paul told the Romans he planned to go on to Spain by way of Rome (Romans 15:24, 28).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Paul stayed a week with disciples at Tyre and visited friends at Sidon (Acts 21:3-4; 27:3).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory in Asia or Oceania with 30,000+ Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country or territory in Asia or Oceania with 30,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.note: Next below the line: Hong Kong, Fiji and Thailand (about 25,000 each), Kiribati (about 23,600).
prompts.summary: The Philippines had about 905,000 Church members at the end of 2025, by far the most in Asia or Oceania. Australia, Japan and New Zealand each had more than 100,000. Samoa, South Korea, Tonga, Taiwan, Papua New Guinea and French Polynesia also had 30,000 or more.

answers.name: French Polynesia
answers.fact: About 30,000 members, just over the line.
